name: Ohana Fiber Mill
old_description: We make quality fiber from local Hawaiian wool, keeping production close to home and connected to the land. Simple, natural, and made with care.
about:
Ohana Fiber Mill operates in Honokaa on the island of Hawaii. The business was started by Alisha and Chris after they made the Big Island their home, driven by a love for the land and a desire to turn local wool into sustainable fiber. No founding year is publicly disclosed.

The mill provides custom fiber processing for customers who supply their own wool, and it produces 100% Hawaiian-grown and processed yarn. It sources Merino, Romney, and other fibers from Kahua Ranch and other small local producers, handling the full wool-to-skein process in a historic, cozy facility. Handmade items are also sold through an on-site retail store.

The company serves local wool producers, fiber artists, makers, and the broader community. Its customer base includes farmers such as Kahua Ranch, crafters seeking custom processing, and visitors looking for locally made yarn and goods.

Ohana Fiber Mill was founded to keep Hawaii's fiber story alive by building a sustainable network connecting land, animals, and people. The founders emphasize connection to the land and the craft community as their guiding purpose.
